title: Only constant spectral weights give a universally conserved energy with the single Maxwell field

rigidity.claim_class: Time-independent functionals H_(w,c) of K1405: one quadratic matter energy weighted by w(Q), c times the existing Maxwell energy and c times the original quartic potential.
rigidity.sufficiency: If w=c on the active Q spectrum, H_(w,c)=c E_mu and is conserved.
rigidity.current_test: Choose smooth finite spectral support and initial electric/matter data with arbitrary nonzero charge-q current. Universal cancellation of integral E dot (j_w-c j_1) forces q(w(q)-c)=0 at every active q!=0.
rigidity.radial_test: Choose two finite charge components and Cauchy velocity with nonzero real radial pairing. Universal cancellation of the quartic defect forces w(q)=c also on neutral components and ties all active components to the same constant.
rigidity.necessity: Because the common core contains arbitrary finite spectral combinations, conservation for every smooth solution implies w(Q)=c I on the full active spectral support.
rigidity.coercivity_consequence: Every unbounded charge-coercive weight, including 1+Q^2 and finite positive polynomials in Q^2, is nonconstant and therefore is not conserved by this single-Maxwell-field quadratic reweighting construction.
rigidity.reopeners: A viable cutoff-uniform mechanism must use additional structure: a nonquadratic or time-dependent correction, a spacetime/null-form estimate, a coupled infinite hierarchy, extra dynamical fields, or another invariant outside H_(w,c).
rigidity.boundary: This is a sharp no-go for the declared functional class, not for all modified energies, normal forms, global completed flows or alternative actions.
